answer: Total inventory value is USD 2,767,451.83 at the stock table's unit cost. This excludes 5 stock lines that have quantity but no cost, so the true figure is higher by an unknown amount.
how_calculated: Sum of LABST * VERPR over ZV_STOCK (1160 rows, unique on MATNR+WERKS+LGORT+CHARG). Check: net of all ZV_MOVEMENT quantities reproduces every ZV_STOCK line (0 mismatches), and valuing those movement-derived quantities at VERPR also gives 2,767,451.83.
assumptions: ZV_STOCK is the current balance by item, warehouse, storage location and lot; no total rows or duplicates found.
VERPR is cost per stock unit: it stays in line with purchase prices and movement unit costs for the same items.
All stock is USD. EA, KG and L are all included because the value is in one currency.
5 lines with blank VERPR are excluded, not valued at zero or estimated.
Blocked items and expired lots are included; items with ACTIVE status alone come to 2,636,862.16.
sql: SELECT WAERS, ROUND(SUM(LABST * VERPR), 2) AS value, SUM(CASE WHEN VERPR IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS lines_without_cost FROM ZV_STOCK GROUP BY WAERS

answer: 585 different items are in stock, out of 600 in the item master.
how_calculated: COUNT(DISTINCT MATNR) on ZV_STOCK. All 1160 lines have LABST above 0, so no zero-quantity lines needed filtering.
assumptions: Different item means a distinct item number (MATNR), not a distinct description; descriptions repeat (249 distinct across 600 items).
Blocked items that hold stock are counted.
sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT MATNR) AS items_in_stock FROM ZV_STOCK WHERE LABST > 0

answer: There are 6 warehouses: 1100, 1110, 1120, 2100, 2110 and 3100. Together they hold 12 storage locations.
how_calculated: Row count of ZV_PLANT (6, unique WERKS). Check: ZV_STOCK also has 6 distinct WERKS.
assumptions: Warehouse means a WERKS in ZV_PLANT; storage locations in ZV_SLOC are sub-areas within them and are not counted as warehouses.

answer: Warehouse 2100 (South Plant — Raw Materials Store) has the highest inventory value: USD 1,128,850.12, 40.79% of the total. The next highest is 1100 at USD 702,920.01.
how_calculated: Sum of LABST * VERPR by WERKS on ZV_STOCK, joined to ZV_PLANT for the name, sorted descending. Check: the six warehouse values add up to the total of 2,767,451.83 within rounding.
assumptions: All stock in USD.

4 lines at 2100 and 1 at 1100 have no cost and are excluded, so those two values are understated. The ranking holds: the 1100 line is worth at most 110.15 at the item's highest movement cost, against a gap of 425,930.11.
Blocked items and expired lots are included.
sql: SELECT s.WERKS, p.NAME1, ROUND(SUM(s.LABST * s.VERPR), 2) AS value FROM ZV_STOCK s JOIN ZV_PLANT p USING (WERKS) GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY value DESC

how_calculated: Sum of LABST * VERPR on ZV_STOCK joined to ZV_MATERIAL where MTART = 'FINISHED' (87 lines). Check: the warehouse breakdown matches, and the four item types add up to the overall total within rounding.
assumptions: Finished goods means item type MTART = 'FINISHED', not everything held in warehouses named Finished Goods. Warehouse 1110 also holds semi-finished stock, which is excluded.
Blocked finished items are included.
None of the finished-goods lines lack a cost.
sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(s.LABST * s.VERPR), 2) AS value, COUNT(*) AS lines, SUM(CASE WHEN s.VERPR IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS no_cost FROM ZV_STOCK s JOIN ZV_MATERIAL m USING (MATNR) WHERE m.MTART = 'FINISHED'

answer: There are 122 A-category items: 118 active and 4 blocked.
how_calculated: Count of ZV_MATERIAL rows where ABCKZ = 'A'; rows and distinct MATNR both give 122. Check: the split by item type (7 + 48 + 12 + 55) and by status (118 + 4) agree.
assumptions: ABCKZ holds the A/B/C category; its only values are A, B and C.
Counted across the item master, whether or not the item currently holds stock.
Blocked items are included.
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_, COUNT(DISTINCT MATNR) AS items FROM ZV_MATERIAL WHERE ABCKZ = 'A'

answer: Raw materials in warehouse 1100 are worth USD 644,081.62. One raw line there has no cost (3114000070, Stretch film 17 µm, 2,164 EA), so this is understated.
how_calculated: Sum of LABST * VERPR on ZV_STOCK joined to ZV_MATERIAL, where WERKS = '1100' and MTART = 'RAW' (283 lines). Check: RAW 644,081.62 plus SEMI 58,838.40 matches warehouse 1100's total of 702,920.01 within rounding.
assumptions: Raw materials means MTART = 'RAW'. Warehouse 1100 also holds SEMI stock, which is excluded despite its name, Raw Materials Store.
The uncosted line is left out, not estimated.
Blocked raw items (69,363.51) are included.
sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(s.LABST * s.VERPR), 2) AS value, COUNT(*) AS lines, SUM(CASE WHEN s.VERPR IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS no_cost FROM ZV_STOCK s JOIN ZV_MATERIAL m USING (MATNR) WHERE s.WERKS = '1100' AND m.MTART = 'RAW'

answer: None: warehouse 1100 holds 0 EA of Pump impeller 175 mm (item 2119000124). This item's stock is at 1120 (17 EA) and 2100 (16 EA), 33 EA in all.
how_calculated: Looked up the item by description in ZV_MATERIAL (exactly one match, 2119000124), then summed LABST by WERKS on ZV_STOCK; there are no rows for 1100. Check: ZV_MOVEMENT has no movements for this item at 1100 at all.
assumptions: The named item is the exact 175 mm description, not similar sizes such as 174 mm or 180 mm.
Warehouse 1100 is WERKS 1100.
No stock row means zero stock, confirmed by the absence of movements.
sql: SELECT '1100' AS warehouse, COALESCE(SUM(LABST), 0) AS qty FROM ZV_STOCK WHERE MATNR = '2119000124' AND WERKS = '1100'

answer: The latest purchase price of item 2119000124 was USD 4,180.2806 per EA, on PO 4500007336 dated 2026-09-28 (17 EA, warehouse 2100, received 2026-10-09).
how_calculated: Took the ZV_PURCHASE line for the item with the latest order date BEDAT. Check: it also has the latest receipt date, the item has no open PO lines, and the matching RECEIPT movement on 2026-10-09 carries the same unit cost, 4180.2806.
assumptions: Latest means most recent purchase order by order date; latest by receipt date gives the same line.
NETPR is price per stock unit (EA), confirmed by the matching receipt movement.
Prices differ by warehouse; the question names none, so this is the latest across all warehouses.
sql: SELECT EBELN, BEDAT, ZZWEDAT, WERKS, MENGE, MEINS, NETPR, WAERS, ZZSTATUS FROM ZV_PURCHASE WHERE MATNR = '2119000124' ORDER BY BEDAT DESC, EBELN DESC LIMIT 1

answer: 80 item and warehouse combinations are below their reorder level: 52 with some stock and 28 with none. 78 of the 80 are active items.
how_calculated: Summed LABST to item + warehouse, because ZV_STOCK splits by storage location and lot, then left-joined from ZV_REORDER (818 unique combinations) and counted stock strictly below MINBE, treating no stock row as 0. Check: 52 with stock plus 28 of the 28 without stock gives 80.
assumptions: MINBE is the reorder level: in all 818 rows it sits between EISBE (safety stock) and MABST (maximum level).
Below is strict; 71 combinations sit exactly at the level and are not counted.
Combinations with a policy but no stock count as below their level.
62 combinations holding stock have no reorder policy and cannot be assessed.
On-order quantity is ignored. Blocked items are included.
sql: WITH s AS (SELECT MATNR, WERKS, SUM(LABST) q FROM ZV_STOCK GROUP BY ALL) SELECT COUNT(*) AS below FROM ZV_REORDER r LEFT JOIN s USING (MATNR, WERKS) WHERE COALESCE(s.q, 0) < r.MINBE

answer: 49 of the 852 item and warehouse combinations holding stock have had no issues in the last 180 days, that is since 2026-05-04. 47 are active items and 2 are blocked.
how_calculated: Distinct item + warehouse pairs in ZV_STOCK, minus pairs with a BWART = 'ISSUE' movement with BUDAT on or after 2026-05-04. Check: a separate LEFT JOIN on last issue date also gives 49.
assumptions: Issue means movement type ISSUE; transfers, adjustments and returns are not issues. Counting TRANSFER_OUT as an issue also gives 49.
The window starts at 2026-10-31 minus 180 days = 2026-05-04; no combination's last issue falls on 2026-05-03 or 2026-05-04, so the boundary does not affect the count.
Issues are matched per warehouse, not across all warehouses.
Every one of these combinations has an earlier issue; none has never had one.
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT MATNR, WERKS FROM ZV_STOCK EXCEPT SELECT DISTINCT MATNR, WERKS FROM ZV_MOVEMENT WHERE BWART = 'ISSUE' AND BUDAT >= DATE '2026-05-04')

answer: 25 distinct lots with stock on hand have already expired. They span 29 stock lines worth USD 10,120.17, with expiry dates from 2025-04-20 to 2026-10-26.
how_calculated: Joined ZV_STOCK lines with a lot to ZV_BATCH on CHARG and counted distinct CHARG with VFDAT before 2026-10-31. Lots rather than lines are counted because one lot can sit in several storage locations. Check: an INTERSECT of stocked lots and expired lots also gives 25.
assumptions: VFDAT is the expiry date: on all 2198 lots that have one, it equals the receipt date ZZWEDAT plus the item's shelf life MHDHB in days.
Expired means VFDAT before today; counting today as well also gives 25.
15 stocked lots have no expiry date and count as not expired.
Item and warehouse agree between stock and lot on every joined line.
sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT s.CHARG) AS expired_lots FROM ZV_STOCK s JOIN ZV_BATCH b ON s.CHARG = b.CHARG WHERE s.LABST > 0 AND b.VFDAT < DATE '2026-10-31'

answer: The top supplier changes with what you mean, so I need to confirm before naming one. All figures are USD MENGE * NETPR from orders dated 2024-10-11 to 2026-10-30. By supplier ID, it is Summit Packaging (0000100013) at 3,726,696.65. Grouping IDs with the same name makes it Vertex Industrial Supply at 4,010,245.67, but its 3 IDs are in 3 countries (JP, DE, US) and may be separate companies. Grouping only same-name, same-country IDs, Summit stays first by 809.77 over Apex Packaging (3,725,886.88), while counting received orders alone puts Apex first by 13,153.60 (3,714,580.51 vs 3,701,426.91). Apex also leads for 2026 to date and the last 12 months under that grouping. Please tell me: should same-name supplier IDs be combined, should open orders count, and over what period?
how_calculated: Summed MENGE * NETPR on ZV_PURCHASE joined to ZV_VENDOR, by LIFNR and by NAME1, for all lines, RECEIVED lines, 2026 orders and orders in the last 12 months. Check: RECEIVED spend of 32,071,624.82 equals the value of RECEIPT movements.
assumptions: ZV_VENDOR has 24 IDs but 19 names, so the supplier grain is itself ambiguous.
No period was given, and the data covers about two years.
Spend is taken from purchase records because no invoice data exists.
sql: SELECT v.NAME1, v.LAND1, COUNT(DISTINCT p.LIFNR) AS ids, ROUND(SUM(MENGE * NETPR), 2) AS all_spend, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN ZZSTATUS = 'RECEIVED' THEN MENGE * NETPR END), 2) AS received FROM ZV_PURCHASE p JOIN ZV_VENDOR v USING (LIFNR) GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY all_spend DESC

answer: There are 43 open purchase order lines.
how_calculated: Count of ZV_PURCHASE rows with ZZSTATUS = 'OPEN'. Check: exactly those 43 rows have no receipt date ZZWEDAT, and all 7654 RECEIVED rows have one.
assumptions: One row is one PO line: EBELN + EBELP is unique.
OPEN means not yet received; the only statuses are OPEN and RECEIVED.
sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS open_lines, COUNT(DISTINCT EBELN || EBELP) AS distinct_lines FROM ZV_PURCHASE WHERE ZZSTATUS = 'OPEN'
